newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Thick EMU fog hides Bel-20 share index potential.
newsitem.headline: Thick EMU fog hides Bel-20 share index potential.

text.p: Belgian shares will reveal their upward scope next week once worries about EMU, rekindled by a close-run French election FR-POL and a tit-for-tat between the German government and the Bundesbank over gold reserves revaluation DE-EMU, will have subsided.

On Thursday the Bel-20 index .BFX fell prey to confusion with Wall Street .DJI indecisive, the dollar steady and bonds weaker. The index, stuck in a tight 11-point range, closed just 0.02 percent lower at 2,257.78 points.
"It should go up, but first we'll have to wait and see what New York and France are going to do," one dealer said.
Business was quiet and cautious. Exceptions included oil firm PetroFina which accounted for more than a quarter of the 3.5 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers said PetroFina, which ended 0.4 percent higher at 12,400, was bound to rise further because its controlling shareholder GBL wanted to see warrants exercised.

The more than one million warrants give holders the right to buy one new PetroFina share at 12,500 francs. They can be exercised until June 3. "There are hedgers on both sides plus the expiry of the warrant," one trader said.
Retailer Delhaize was a notable gainer, up 1.2 percent at 1,740 francs, collecting a respectable volume of 127,486 shares despite a lack of news from its U.S. unit Food Lion or the dollar.
Traders said Delhaize's slide on Wednesday had been caused by one large brokerage. "It was simply exaggerated and now it's coming back," one said.
Fellow retailer GIB was the main riser, up 1.6 percent at 1,545. One trader said it had been seriously lagging the market. "It has enormous scope if its turnaround succeeds," he said.
